fr.elements: Main Building; Front Driveway; Access Road; Open Green Space; Landscaped Area; Detached Structure; Perimeter Fencing; Open Terrain; Street Frontage; Vehicle Parking Area
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Open Terrain; Limited Rear Access
fr.recommendations: Ensuring the single access point and extended driveway remain clear of parked vehicles and other obstructions could significantly improve apparatus entry and exit during an emergency response. Posting visible address markers at the street frontage and at the driveway entrance may assist responding units in locating the property quickly, particularly during low-visibility conditions. Maintaining adequate turning and staging space near the main building and detached structure would support simultaneous multi-unit operations. Given the limited rear access, communicating the property layout to the local fire agency in advance could facilitate pre-incident planning and improve operational effectiveness upon arrival.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Continuous Shrub Cover; Scattered Shrubs; Heavy Ground Vegetation; Fuel Continuity; Brush Adjacent to Structure; Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Wildland Interface; Open Terrain; Isolated Structure; Vegetated Access Route; Brushland Interface
wildfire.recommendations: Reducing the continuity of shrub cover surrounding the structure and creating separation between brush and the building perimeter would improve defensible space and reduce opportunities for fire to reach the structure. Where shrubs are adjacent to the structure, clearing or thinning vegetation to establish a buffer zone around the foundation, walls, and any attached features may reduce direct fuel contact and support suppression operations. Managing heavy ground vegetation within the immediate structure zone could further reduce fuel continuity across the property. Maintaining the access route by reducing vegetation encroachment along its edges would support firefighter access and improve conditions for emergency response and evacuation. Given the isolated nature of the structure within open terrain at the wildland interface, sustaining a well-managed perimeter of reduced fuels around the structure and keeping the access route clear of overhanging or encroaching vegetation would contribute meaningfully to long-term wildfire resilience and property preparedness.
